title: Marvelous Designer to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content: This guide outlines the workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0-Xj3E11GzM Step 1. Import USD Asset Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman Step 3. Create Cloth Asset Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset Step 5. Organize Assets Step 6. Create Outfit Asset Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility * * * ## Step 1. Import USD Asset ## ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018460697) 1. In the **Content Drawer** , import your Clothing USD Asset created in Marvelous Designer into the desired folder. 2. Verify that the static meshes are correctly imported. ## Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018466585) 1. Locate your MetaHuman in the **Content Browser**. * Or, run it through the right-click Context Menu → MetaHuman → MetaHuman Character to create a new MetaHuman 2. **Double-click** the MetaHuman to open the **MetaHuman Editor**. 3. Export the MetaHuman as a **Combined Skeletal Mesh** : * MetaHuman Editor Main Menu → MetaHuman Creator → Export Combined Skel Mesh * Save this mesh inside the **Skeletal Meshes** folder of your USD asset directory. ## Step 3. Create Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799079787033) 1. In the **Static Meshes** folder: * **Right-click** → **Physics > Cloth Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., CA_name). 2. **Open Cloth Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Right-click the Cloth Asset → **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. 3. **Clean up nodes** : * Delete everything except: * USD Import * Transfer Skin Weights * Remesh * Remesh LOD2 (optional for extra LOD) * Cloth Asset Terminal. ## Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799641793433) 1. **Add Static Mesh Import Node** : * Right-click background → **Create Node: Static Mesh Import**. * Assign your USD static mesh to this node. 2. **Connect Nodes** : * Static Mesh Import → Transfer Skin Weights. * Transfer Skin Weights → Cloth Asset Terminal. * Also connect: * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh → Collection LOD0. * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh LOD2 → Cloth Asset Terminal (optional). 3. **Configure Transfer Skin Weights Node** : * Target Meshes: **Render Mesh**. * Render Mesh Transfer: **Skeletal Mesh**. * Transform Method: **Closest Point on Surface**. * Assign the **Combined Skeletal Mesh** to the Skeletal Mesh property. 4. **Preview** : * Switch the left window view to **Render** for visualization. ## Step 5. Organize Assets ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881262873) 1. Create a new folder inside the Basic**Mesh** folder. 2. Move: * Static Mesh * Cloth Asset * Cloth Asset Node into this folder. ## Step 6. Create Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881264409) 1. In **Static Mesh Folder** : * **Right-click** → **Physics > Outfit Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., OA_name). 2. Select **Resizable Outfit Template** when prompted. 3. Move the Outfit Asset node into the folder created earlier. ## Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581027609) 1. **Open Outfit Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Double-click the Outfit Asset. 2. Change **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** from **Automatic** to **Manual**. 3. **Add Source Asset** : * Select **Sized Outfit Source** → Click **+**. * Drag the Cloth Asset into the Source Asset option. * Assign a size name. 4. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** and wait for completion. 5. Open **Source Body Slider** : * Drag and drop the Combined Skeletal Mesh. 6. Enable **Sized Outfit** checkbox to make it resizable. 7. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** again, then switch back to **Automatic**. ## Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581029657) 1. Open MetaHuman Editor. 2. Go to the **Hair and Clothing** tab. 3. Drag and drop the **Outfit Asset** from the Content Drawer into the Outfit Clothing section. 4. In the Body tab, change the model's size parameters to adjust MetaHuman proportions, and confirm that the outfit adapts dynamically. 5. **Verify** that the outfit adjusts automatically to match the Metahuman's new size. ## ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility The use of ChaosCloth assets from USD data exported from Marvelous Designer is subject to the following compatibility restrictions based on the Unreal Engine version: * **Marvelous Designer 2025.0:** Compatible only with **UE 5.4**. * **Marvelous Designer 2025.2:** Compatible with **UE 5.6** and later version. * **UE 5.5:** Not compatible due to technical issues regarding simulation data. ※ Note: This issue is specific to **ChaosCloth**. Regular meshes and materials are unaffected.
content_description: This guide provides a comprehensive workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD files and seamlessly integrating them with Unreal Engine's MetaHuman for enhanced character customization.

title: USD file Compatibility (ver. 12.1)
content: ## Feature Overview With USD, a graphics standard file format, you can increase collaboration productivity with a variety of 3D software You can export clothing, avatars, and accessories with meshes and materials from Marvelous Designer as USD files. You can also import USD files created in other 3D software packages into Marvelous Designer. ## Import USD You can import an USD file as an avatar, a trim, or a scene/prop type. Cloth and avatar animations can also be exported/imported. (ver. 2024.1) ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below. **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add)▶ USD USD Layer Window ▶ Import Drag & drop an USD file on to the software **Setting - Import USD Dialog** Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported file only. ---|---|--- Add | Add an object, keeping the existing objects. Object Type | Avatar | Import an USD file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import an USD file as a Trim type. \- The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. \- Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. \- Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. \- Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scenes & Props | When importing an object as Scenes & Props, the object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Scenes & Props type do not have Collision. Auto Create Fitting Suit | A Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Scale | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver.2024.1) | X, Y(Up), Z | Using Axis Conversion, you can change the orientation of the imported mesh. Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. Invert | Invert the selected axis. Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. ※ Note (ver. 2024.1): * It is recommended that the Animation Layer name not be changed. * When importing an Avatar that is a USD file format, [Motion files (.MTN)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358363172249) cannot be applied to that avatar because it is not the default skeletal avatar type supported by Marvelous Designer. * If multiple skeletal animations (SkelAnimation) are loaded into the animation window, the upper most animation is played in the 3D Space. ### End Result The USD file is successfully imported into the software you set. A list of layers for the imported file can be found on the USD Layer window. \- If USD Layer window is not visible in the workspace, it will appear in a new window as a pop-up. ## Export USD You can export clothing, avatars or trims as an USD file. Cloth and avatar animations can also be exported. (ver. 2024.1) ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below: **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD **Setting - Export USD Dialog** Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Select All Patterns | Either select or deselect all patterns. -Each pattern can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Select All Avatars | Either select or deselect all avatars/objects \- Each avatar/object can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Select All Graphics and Trims | Either select or deselect all graphics and trims \- Each graphic and trim can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Single Object (ver. MD2024.0) | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects (ver. MD2024.0) | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Option (Ver. 2024.1) | Garment Animation (Ver. 2024.1) | Saves pattern cache animation. ※ Note : Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation (Ver. 2024.1) | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. ※ Note : Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache (ver. 2024.2) | Saves Avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver. 2024.2) | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. ### ※ Note (Ver. 2024.1): * It is recommended that the Animation Layer name not be changed. * To export a pattern and an avatar at the same time, select the avatar first and then select the patterns. ### End Result The USD file is successfully exported as you set. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. ## USD Layer Window A list of layers for the imported file can be found in the USD Layer window. ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below: **Location** The drop-down list at the top center of all windows. ▶ USD Layer ![usd_layer_window.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438538423577) **1\. Buttons** Create | Create an USD file \- An USD file is created with the specified path and name, appearing in the USD Layer window. This file will be set as the Authoring Layer. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. ---|--- Import | Import an USD file Clear | Delete all the layers listed in the USD Layer. **2\. List of Layers** Authoring Layer | The default layer which is being used at the moment. \- When running Export to USD Layer for clothing, trims, scenes/props, they will be exported to the Authoring Layer. ---|--- Material | The default path where the Materials appear. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. Mesh | The default path where the Mesh appears. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. **3\. Right Mouse Button****Menus - Layers** Click the right mouse button on the list of the layers to access the menus below. ![usd_layer_window2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438532533785) Set Authoring Layer | Set the selected layer as active. \- The same can be done by double clicking the left mouse button** **This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is already set as the Authoring Layer. \- Where the selected layer is an USDZ (read only) \- Where the selected layer is missing. ---|--- Delete | Deleted the selected layer. This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is the Authoring Layer. Export USDZ from Layer | Export the selected layer as USDZ (read only) \- Once an USDZ is imported, it cannot be exported again. **4\. Export the Selected Object through Right Mouse Button Menus** To export your cloth and/or trim assets from Marvelous Designer as a USD file; select the assets from either 3D or 2D window, and click "Export to USD Layer" to export them to the Authoring Layer. This will update the USD file corresponding to the Authoring Layer. **Setting - Export to USD Layer** Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Single Object (ver. 2024.0) | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects (ver. 2024.0) | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin (ver. 2024.2) | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick (ver. 2024.2) | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data (ver. 2024.2) | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Option (Ver. 2024.1) | Cache Animation (ver. 2024.1) | Saves pattern cache animation. ※ Note : Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation (ver. 2024.1) | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. ※ Note : Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache (ver. 2024.2) | Saves avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver. 2024.2) | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. * When exporting garment using Export to USD Layer, the exported output will differ depending on the 3D Garment Rendering Style state. If the 3D garment appears in Thick Textured Surface, it will be exported with thickness. ### End Result The USD file is successfully exported as you set it. * When saving the project file (*.zprj), the imported USD Layer and file information will be saved altogether. \- When opening this file, if the USD file path is missing, you can either create new or ignore it. Create new USD file path in replace of the missing one, using the right mouse button menus. * Please try out this **[USD sample file](https://s3.marvelousdesigner.com/newmdweb/helpcenter/manual/KoiFish_USD.zip) **we created with Marvelous Designer and see how the new USD support can benefit your workflow. Step by step tutorial for how to export this USD file from Marvelous Designer coming soon.
content_description: Discover how to seamlessly import and export USD files in Marvelous Designer, enhancing your workflow for 3D clothing, avatars, and accessories.

title: Modular Library (Ver. 2025.0)
content: **Table of Contents** Modular Library (2025.0) Structure of The Modular Library Group and Category Line Style Block Auto Modular Labeling Modular Configurator Save Style Save Block Modular Library Options ### YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FHl1WI9VMgQ ### ## Modular Library ### Objective Quickly and easily create different variations using previously saved garment blocks within Marvelous Designer. This section contains all of your blocks for mixing and matching different styles. Here you can also create and save: Groups, Categories, Styles, and Blocks. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Modular Library Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown Menu ▶ Modular Library ※Note: The buttons on the top right are: * **Add** (to add in a new Group or Category) * **List** (To switch between a list and icons) * **Refresh** (update to view any changes) #### ![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881) #### Structure of the Libraries By default, the Modular Library is organized by**Group, Category** and**Style.** This is where all of your blocks will be to mix and match different styles and blocks, here you can also create and save groups, categories, styles and blocks. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143614745)** **Group and Category** Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. **![Modular Library.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143616409)** Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. 1. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button to add your folder to a Group. 2. Doble-click the Group folder to navigate into the Category. 3. in Category stage, click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button and enter the name to add a new category. _**✨Tip:**_ You can copy the path or delete by right-clicking on a Group or Category folder. ### **![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881)** ## Group and Category ### Objective Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. ### Operation ### Adding a New Group or Category 1. Click the Add (plus) button on the top Right, and click Add Group. Select the folder you want to add. → The selected folder will be added as a group. 2. Double-click the added group folder, and click the Add (plus) button on the top of the category tab and click Add Category. → The Add Category window appears. 3. Enter the category name and click the OK button. → The category is added to the selected group. ### Editing Group or Category 1. Select the folder you want to edit and Right click to see your options 1. Copy the Path → Path to the explorer folder is copied. 2. Delete → The folder is deleted. ### ## Line _This is an optional sub-category or "stage" between Category and Style._ Add a Line tier between Category and Style to create a more precise and detailed library structure. 1. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button in the Style stage and click **Group Style by Line** option. 2. In Add Line window, set the name and thumbnail and click **OK** button. → It becomes the upper level above Style in the hierarchy. This allows multiple styles to be grouped under a Line. 3. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button on the right side of the Line to add another Line. _**✨Tip:**_ When clicking **Add Line with Same Style** option, all Styles and Blocks within the selected Line are duplicated and added as a new Line. This can be useful when you want to reuse the same structure but make slight changes to some Styles or Blocks. 4. Right-click on the Line thumbnail to delete the selected Line or, change its thumbnail and name. #### ## ** **Style The style is the what all your blocks will be linked to. It is best to think of the different styles as a type of fit so that all your blocks can easily fit together when mixing and matching different blocks. #### ※ Note: The name of the group and category that this style is saved in, is at the top left. ![Modular Library1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438081751833) ### Adding Style 1. After making Category, you can create Style. Double-click the category folder in which you want to add a style, and click the Add button on the top of the style tab. → Style Section window appears. → If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. 2. If you want to register thumbnail manually, click the camera icon and open the image file. 3. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. → Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. ### Editing Style 1. 1. Select the Style you want to edit and Right Click → The Style Selection pop up will come up again and allow you to change the Thumbnail, and Style Name. 2. Delete → If there are blocks within this style a Warning will pop up that the blocks included will be erased and to ask if you would still like to proceed. ![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881) ## Block These are the different pattern pieces that make up one full style. You can add in multiple patterns for one block, they will be what you will use to mix and create different variations of a style. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438050383641) #### Adding a Block Section ※Note: For automatic block creation, please refer to the "Auto Block Creation" section below. 1. Click the thumbnail of the style that you want to add block, then click the Add (plus) icon and click Add Block Type on the top right. → Create Add Block Type window appears. ※ Note: Style needs to be added in order to add Block. 2. After setting the information below, click the OK button. Type | Set the block type ---|--- Tag | Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten. → the block type is added to the selected style. ### Adding a Pattern to a Block Section 1. 1. Within the added Block Section select the Add (plus) icon. → A Modular Creator pop up window will appear. 2. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. → To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key → Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board 3. The Block Section window will pop up → The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window → If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select the camera icon to create New Thumbnail 4. The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library ### Additional Options 1. Right-Click the block thumbnail you want to edit 2. Select the appropriate menu options as needed. Delete Selected Block | Deletes the selected Block. ---|--- Share Selected Block | Share the selected block with other styles. Any changes made to the block will apply to all shared instances. Change Thumbnail | Change the thumbnail. Replace with New Block | Replace the existing block with a new one. ### Auto Modular Labeling Auto Modular Labeling is based on the results learned from numerous pattern data and analyzes which part of the pattern it is based on only the shape of the pattern. 1. Click ![AI Active.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036889369) **Auto Modular Labeling** button at the top right of the Style stage. → The automatically recognized blocks will be highlighted in colors corresponding to each block type. ![Modular Library3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143655449) 2. Check all that all patterns in the 2D window are properly assigned to the correct block types using the Modular Creator. 2-1. If any patterns are not recognized correctly, you can manually adjust or relabel them by clicking **![edit.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157792665)Edit Block** button in the Modular Creator. 2-2. In the 2D window, select the patterns that match the block type you chose and then press the Enter key. _* You can select multiple patterns by holding the Shift key. _ 2-3. In Add Block File window, set the name and thumbnail and click**OK** button. _* The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window._ 3. Click ![Button-1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157793945) **Save Block** button to set thumbnail image and file name, then click **OK** button. → The Check mark will then be activated to signal that this block is ready. 4. Click**Add** button. 5. After checking whether the block pattern is sewn well with other block patterns, click **OK** button. _* If you need to reset the sewing line, click the Cancel button to correct the sewing line and try again._ ※Note: If you are adding a new block based on an existing block file, you can add it directly without going through the Modular Creator by clicking ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) Add button within each Block section, such as Front Body or Sleeves. ### ### ## Modular Configurator This is specifically for saving out style or blocks. This method brings you directly to the Modular Creator which makes saving out styles or blocks a little quicker. #### ### Save Style: 1. Select the Group & Category to save this style under → Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top 2. Select the Add button to add a new Style 3. The Style Section Window will appear → If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. 4. If you want to register thumbnail manually, select Create New Thumbnail and open the image file. 5. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. → Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. #### ### Save Block: 1. Select the Group & Category to save this style under → Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top 2. Select the Style to save the blocks under → Can also create a new style using the add button at the top 3. Add in the Block Type using the Add button at the top ※Note: Can also use the Auto Block Creation tool this will automatically add in all the blocks and assign all patterns to the coinciding blocks 4. Create New Block Type window appears. → After setting the information below, click the OK button. **Type** | Set the block type ※Note:→ the block type is added to the selected style. ---|--- **Tag** | Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten 5. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. → To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key → Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board 6. The Block Section window will pop up. → The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window → If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select create New Thumbnail. 7. The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library. ## ## Modular Library Options Here is where you can configure Modular setting / options. 1. Click Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Preferences ▶ Other in the top menu. Configure Modular Options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Default Folder** | Set the default location that the Modular Library saves the Style presets to. **Modular Access** | **Protect Modular Library to Restrict Editing** | Restrict all editing in the Modular Library to protect its original configuration. **Prevent Blocks Mix and Match across Different Styles** | To protect the users from apply different block fits together, turn on the option Prevent Mix and Match. When Prevent Mix and Match is active a Warning pop up will appear when a block from one style is being applied to a separate style. **Notch Sewing** | To save out a specific sewing relationship activate the Notching Sewing option. The Modular Sewing tags will then follow the notch placements for sewing relationships.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for utilizing the Modular Library in Marvelous Designer, enabling users to efficiently create, organize, and save garment variations through customizable blocks, styles, and categories.

title: ZIPPER: Edit Zipper
content: ## Objective Edits the length of the zipper. ## Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ **Edit Zipper** 3D Toolbar ▶ **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51994437007257) Edit Zipper** ## ## Operation 1. Click the tool or menu in Location. 2. Click the end point of the zipper and drag in direction to be edited, 3. Then release the mouse to confirm the position. 4. D the end point of the opposite zipper and drag it the same way. → A **blue dot** appears when the length matches the one modified on the opposite side. 5. Then release the mouse to confirm the position. 6. Both lengths of the zipper are modified.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for editing the length of a zipper in the 3D design tool.

title: Pleats
content: ## **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Pleats.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51784511607961)Pleats** ## **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- **Specification** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. **※ Note:** * If the segment where pleats are to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn in place based on the pleat type selected. If the segment is not sewn, use the **Pleats Sewing** tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern. * Pleats are dependent on segment point locations. When a pleat is started between two segment points, it will not go further than the next segment point and will result in an error/ red color to indicate this.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and customizing pleats in 2D patterns using the Pleats tool in the design software.

title: MetaHuman DNA Importer
content: ## **Objective** [**MetaHuman**](https://www.metahuman.com/en-US) is a next-generation digital human creation technology introduced by Epic Games, offering ultra-realistic character modeling and rigging that are almost indistinguishable from reality. Based on high-resolution 3D scans of real people, it enables precise expression of facial features, skin textures, hair, and body proportions, and works seamlessly with **Unreal Engine** for use in films, games, virtual fittings, and more. Now, **Marvelous Designer** allows direct import of **MetaHuman DNA data** , enabling garment creation that reflects realistic facial structures and body proportions with exceptional accuracy. ※ Note: DNA is the file format (*.dna) used for MetaHuman data. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import/Import(Add) ▶ DNA ## **Operation** 1. Prepare the Body and Head files (*.dna) extracted from the MetaHuman Editor (Unreal Engine). 2. Go to **File** ▶ **Import/Import (Add)** ▶**DNA** to open the **MetaHuman DNA Importer** dialog. 3. Load both the Body and Head DNA files. 4. Set the additional import options 5. A seamless MetaHuman combining the Head and Body will be loaded as an Avatar type. ## **Options** Options | Description ---|--- **File** | **Body** | Load the Body file of the MetaHuman. **Head** | Load the Head file of the MetaHuman. **Basic** | **Unit** | Select the desired unit and enter the scale as a numerical value. **Options** | **Auto Add Arrangement Points** | For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. **Auto Create Fitting Suit** | For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. **Axis Conversion** | Modifying Object's Axis direction. ※ Note: * Enable **Avatar Display** ▶**Show Avatar Joint** to control the pose in your desired form. * Create animations by setting keyframes on the joints. * Applying motion files(*.mtn) is not supported.
content_description: Discover how to seamlessly import and utilize MetaHuman DNA data in Marvelous Designer for creating ultra-realistic garments that perfectly match digital human features.

title: Convert Pattern to: Trim, Accessory
content: ## **Objective** Allows converting patterns into Trim or Accessory types. ## **Location** 3D Pattern Context Menu ▶ Convert ▶ to Trim 3D Pattern Context Menu ▶ Convert ▶ to Avatar Accessory ## **Operation** #### **Convert to Trim** 1. Select a 3D pattern and right-click to open the context menu. 2. Execute **Convert** ▶**to Trim**. 3. The pattern is converted into a Trim and registered under Trim Style. #### **Convert to Avatar Accessory** 1. Select a 3D pattern and right-click to open the context menu. 2. Execute **Convert** ▶******to Avatar Accessory.** 3. The pattern is converted into an Avatar Accessory, and the **Register Accessory** dialog appears. 4. Configure options such as **Accessory Type** , then save the file in ***** **.zacs** format.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for converting 3D patterns into Trim or Avatar Accessory types using the context menu options.

title: ZIPPER: Zipper/Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
content: ### Objective Modify the Zipper or Slider via the right-click pop-up menu. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Right-Click on a Zipper or Slider ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Right-Click on a Zipper or Slider → The respective pop-up menu appears for the Zipper or Slider. 2. Adjust the settings below as needed: Option | Zipper Tape | Slider ---|---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected Zipper and Zipper Slider. **Deactivate** | Deactivate or activate the selected Zipper and Slider. **Freeze** | Freeze or unfreeze the selected Zipper and Slider. **Reverse** **(Right-Clicked Teeth)** | Reverse the sewing direction of the Zipper Tape based on the side of the Zipper Tape that was right clicked. | n/a **Flip Normal** **(Right-Clicked Teeth)** | Flip the surface of the side of the Zipper Tape that was right clicked. | n/a **Flip (Selected)** | n/a | Flip the selected object. **Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern** | Automatically duplicates the selected zipper to the corresponding symmetric position. **Reset Slider Arrangement** | n/a | Reset the slider's position and angle to default (ver4.1.0). **Show/Hide** | n/a | Show or hide the Zipper components * Slide * Puller * Top Stopper * Bottom Stopper

title: Simulation
content: ### ### Objective Use this function to apply gravity and drape the 3D Garments in the 3D Garment window. Pressing the Simulate button causes all 3D Garments to fall toward the floor and drape onto Avatars and similar objects with collision that are in the way. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Simulate** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Simulate** ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Simulate** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Simulate** →3D Garments in the 3D window drapes on Avatars. →When the Simulation is activated, the tool automatically switches to the **Select/Move** tool (ver5.1.0.) **※Note:** * Simulation presets are added to the 3D toolbar (ver. 4.2.0). Long press the Simulate tool icon to access the additional options. Name | Description ---|--- **Normal (Default)** | Select Simulate(Normal) when working on a 3D Garment. \- When the simulation preset is set to Simulate(Normal), You can work on the 3D Garment efficiently with the fastest simulation speed setting. **Animation (Stable)** | Garment simulation is more defined with higher simulation quality settings, the simulation speed will likely decrease. \- Use this preset when recording animation caches. **Fitting** **(Accurate Fabric)** | Garment simulation is more defined and fabric stretch is expressed more realistically, this is the slowest but most accurate to real world simulation setting. **Processor** | **CPU** | CPU based simulation. **GPU** | GPU based simulation. Depending on the computer specification, the simulation speed can increase. ※ Note: GPU simulation feature is greatly improved in (ver. 2024.2) with same collision handing accuracy as CPU simulation. The results from CPU and GPU based simulations are matched, with minimal differences. **※ Note:** * Users can select CPU/GPU from simulation toolbar with different simulation presets. (ver. 2024.2) * Animation (Stable) is added into Simulation Toolbar. Users may opt to run simulations prior to recording an animation. (ver. 2024.2) * **GPU acceleration for Trim Simulation and Soft Body Simulation are limited in the current version.** (ver. 2024.2) * Adjustments to 2D Patterns' points and segments are reflected in the 3D window in real-time (ver. 4.2.0). The real-time Simulation (Interactive Editing) is unavailable from Marvelous Designer ver. 4.2.0's last patch. * Even during heavy computational load, the simulation can be stopped instantly. (ver. 2025.2)
content_description: This web page provides instructions and options for simulating gravity and draping 3D garments in the 3D Garment window, enhancing the realism of garment interactions with avatars and other objects.

title: Pins
content: ### Objective Create, Delete, and other functions relating to Pin tool. * Create Pin * Delete Pin * Duplicate Pins To Symmetric Pattern * Attach / Detach Pins from Avatar ## Create Pin ### Objective Affix specific portions of the Garment and utilize Pin similar to the Freeze function. It is also convenient when turning/flipping over collars, lapels, or cuffs. ### Location #### Pin Tool Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click for more than 2 seconds) ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) #### Select/Move Tool Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### Pin Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click more than 2 seconds) ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) → The Garment mesh is now displayed in red in both the 3D and 2D windows. 2. Click on a vertex (a point of the mesh). → A Pin is created on the selected point. 3. Or click on a desired area on the Garment ▶ Click and drag to select the area. → Pins are created on the vertex of the selected area. → Pins can also be created on 2D Patterns. 4. Click and drag, or use the Gizmo to move the pinned mesh as desired in the 3D window. ※ Note: Click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Shift + Ctrl on the keyboard to create additional pinned areas. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Ctrl on the keyboard to remove Pins from existing pinned areas. #### Select/Move Tool 1. Click on the Select/Move tool in the 3D window. 2. Click while pressing W on the keyboard to create a Pin on a specific point. → A Pin is created on the selected point. 3. If the input language is set to Korean, a Pin cannot be created when pressing W on the keyboard. Make sure to change the input language to English. ※ Note: * #### Create Pin on Segment Double-click on a Pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a segment. When creating Pins on the Pattern in the 2D window, Pins are generated on adjacent segment vertices when the angle difference is less than 20˚. * #### Create Pin on Pattern Double-click on a Pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a Pattern. * #### Create Pin on Internal Line (ver4.0.0) Use the same procedure as above to create Pins on specific Internal Lines and Shapes. * #### Select All Pins on the Same Pattern (ver 2025.2) Double-clicking a created Pin selected all Pins placed on the same pattern at once. ## Delete Pin ### Objective Delete unnecessary pins. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins → The selected pin is now being deleted. ※ Note: Selecting a created pin while holding W key on keyboard also deletes the pin. ## Duplicate Pins To Symmetric Pattern (ver. 2024.2) ### Objective Added the ability to reflect pins onto the symmetric pattern, including all pin details such as pin position. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) ### Operation 1. Create pins by following guideline in the**Location** above. 2. In 3D window, right-click on the Pin/Pins in the scene. 3. Click the option "Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern" 4. Duplicate Pin/Pins are created on the other side of the Symmetric pattern with all the pin details including the position of the Pin/Pins 5. When Simulating, both sides will be Symmetrical with Pins. ※ Note: * If a pattern with no symmetry is selected, and trying to apply this ‘Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern’ option. A pop-up box will appear with error message: “Some Pattern/Patterns has no symmetry applied. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern can only be applied to pattern with Symmetry“ * If a set of pins on multiple patterns is added and some of them have Symmetry and the others don't. The function will apply pins only on the respective symmetric pattern with the above pop-up message box. ## Attach / Detach Pins from Avatar ### Objective Affix specific parts of the Garments to the Avatar. This function is commonly used for Simulation or recording animation for avoiding the Garment sliding off from the Avatar. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) ### Operation #### Attach Pin to Avatar 1. Create a pin to attach to an Avatar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) 3. Right-click on the created pin ▶ select Attach Pin to Avatar/Attach All Pins to Avatar. → The selected pin is now being attached to the nearest part of the Avatar. ※ Note: Pins attached to the Avatar are unable to be selected or moved. #### Detach Pin from Avatar 1. Right-click on the pin attached to the avatar ▶ select Detach from Avatar/Detach All Pins from Avatar. → The attached pin is now being detached from the Avatar.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide comprehensive guidance on using the Pin tool for creating, deleting, and managing pins on garments, including instructions for attaching pins to avatars and duplicating pins to symmetric patterns.

title: User Interface (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software in User Settings. Designated settings will become the default after the program is restarted. Shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. Modify UI related settings in the User Interface section. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ User Interface Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ User Interface (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Adjust the settings below as needed: Unit | Set the measurement unit (inch, centimeter, millimeter) for the program. The software must be restarted for the changes to apply. ---|--- Use Ligne (L) for Button Width | Toggle this option on to adjust button size in ligne (v4.0.0). Default Topstitch Thread Thickness Unit(ver4.2.0) | Choose the default unit for thread thickness (ver4.2.0). Toolbar | 3D Toolbar | Organize the 3D toolbar in the top, bottom, right, or left side of the window (ver4.0.0). 2D Toolbar | Organize the 2D toolbar in the top, bottom, right, or left side of the window (ver4.0.0). Group Tools (ver. 5.1.431) | Group tools of the same category. Activate this option to minimize the problem of hidden tools when using the standard layout. ※Note: All manuals are written with an underlying assumption that the Group Tools option is activated. **Appearance** | Line | **Pattern Outline** : Outline color of 2D Patterns. **Internal Line** : Color of 3D/2D Internal Lines. **Wireframe** : Wireframe color of 3D Patterns. **Selected** : Outline color of the selected object. **Hover** : Outline color of the hovered object. **Font Size** : Font size of 2D Measurements Thickness | **Thickness (Pixels)** : Outline thickness of 2D Patterns. Highlight | **3D Pattern** : Color displayed on selected 3D Patterns. **Freeze** : Color of frozen 3D Patterns. **Strengthen** : Color of 3D Patterns with Strengthen applied. **Layer** : Color of 3D Patterns with Layer applied. **Bond** : Color of 3D/2D Patterns with Bond applied. **Solidify** : Color of 3D Patterns with Solidify applied. **Font** | Font Type | Select the desired font type. Resolution | Automatically Scale Display (ver4.2.0) | When the option is on, the resolution automatically adjusts to the monitor's resolution. title: Freeze/Unfreeze
content: ### Objective Use this function to fasten Patterns like solid objects. For example, deactivated Patterns do not collide during Simulation; however, frozen Patterns do. Therefore it is better to use it for draping multiple layered Garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner Garments first, then draping outerwear simultaneously, solves the occasional instabilities. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Freeze / Unfreeze ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Freeze / Unfreeze → The selected Pattern is now being frozen/unfrozen. ※ Note: * 3D Statement * Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu ▶ Show/Hide Color [(Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358311619225)[ ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/32523191112473/preview/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpZCI6MzI1MjMxOTExMTI0NzMsImV4cCI6MTcxNTk3NDk0Mn0.vTz8AEFpwglRHaNeFb09thKYnyuNna7SAvTfH7sSS8U)to hide the Freeze color display in the 3D window.

title: Print on Fabric
content: **List of Contents** Add Print Print Properties Copy Print Print various patterns on Fabric. ### **Add Print** 1. Click **Add Print** to the right of the Fabric in Fabric tab of the Object Browser. 2. Select the desired image. → A print item is added under the fabric item. ### **Print Properties** 1. Click the Print Item under the Fabric item. → Print Properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Edit the Print Properties as needed. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | Name the print by clicking the name of the fabric item or right-clicking on it and select Rename. You can also change the name in the Property Editor. **Configuration** | **Face** | Set the orientation(Front, Back, and Both) of the fabric to be printed. **Repeat Type** | Set the Repeat Type (Block, Half Drop, Brick, Diamond, Stripe)of the pattern to be printed **Space** | Set the space between the images of the X / Y-axis. **Shift** | Shift the images along the X / Y-axis. **Material** | **Use Same PBR Maps as Fabric** **(ver 2025.1)** | The fabric’s PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness) are automatically applied and blended with the print. Alternatively, you can apply specific maps selectively by enabling the ‘Use the same map as the fabric’ option for each map. **Type** | Set the Type of Print Image. If you set the option to use the same normal map as the fabric, the normal map of the fabric is also applied to the print. **Transformation** | Set the width, height and angle of the Print Image. Edit Texture tool edits the texture of the fabric and the print image together and if the fabric to which the print image was added has no texture, the Texture Editor tool cannot be used **Open/Save** | Print Properties can be saved or opened as a PRT file. When saving as a fabric file(ZFAB), the print properties are also saved.

title: Denim Wet Wash Effect
content: **New in 2025.1** Apply Wash Parameters **** Express Denim wet wash effects without using external software and avoid many back-and-forth steps. #### **Apply** 1. Change the Material Type to the**Denim** → It is applied as unwashed by default. 2. Apply the denim texture as the Base Color Map. 3. Set the Denim **Wet Process** type. → The wash effects are applied on the Fabric's Base Color Map. 4. Assign the **Wash Map** and adjust the **Wash Parameters** to achieve the desired result. #### **Wash Parameters** Adjust the wash parameters to express realistic wet wash effects. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Wet Process** | **Wash Map** | Apply a texture map to achieve the wash effect. **Transformation** | Scale, rotate or move the Wash Effect **Softerners/Enzyme Concentration/** **FadingIntensity/** **Concentration/Map Intensity** | Set the wash effect intensity on the Base Color Map. **Blend** | Plenty of Blending options are provided, which decide how the wash effect blends with the base Fabric. _* Overlay is recommended for the majority of Denim washes._ **Absorbency** | Adjust how deeply these effects need to be absorbed/spread in the Base Fabric. * Keep the Absorbency minimal(0~20) with the seamless wash effect map to avoid repeat issue **Cycle Duration** | Sets the Cycle Duration/Washing Time. Longer duration removes more dye/color from the yarn (Base Color Map). **Seam Abrasion** | Enhance the Base Color Map of Puckering applied to the pattern with the respective Fabric.
content_description: Discover the new 2025.1 feature that simplifies the application of realistic wet wash effects on denim, streamlining your workflow without the need for external software.

title: Import and Export Preset
content: **New in MD 2025.1** **Add Preset** **Preset Options** **Supported File Formats** When Importing or Exporting 3D files, users can save their configured options as a preset for reuse. These preset files can also be shared, allowing users to distribute organizational standards and policies. #### #### Add Preset 1. Go to **File > Import/Export** to import 3D file. 2. Configure the desired options in the Import dialog. 3. Click the **Preset > ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48920118220057)Add **button at the top of the dialog. 4. In the **Create Configuration** dialog, set the **Preset Path** and **Name**. 5. Click Save button to store the preset. The saved preset will then be selected in the Preset dropdown. * The saved preset can be selected during future imports to consistently apply the configured settings * Default Path: C:\Users\Public\Documents\MarvelousDesigner\Configuration\Preset\Import #### #### Preset Options **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Add** | Add a new preset. **Remove** | Delete the currently selected preset. **Open Folder** | Open the folder where the currently selected preset is saved. #### #### Supported File Formats Only 3D file formats are supported * OBJ, FBX, Alembic, USD * Maya Cache (MC, MCX), Point Cache 2, MDD Cache (Standard, Maya/3ds Max), OBJ Sequence **📝 Note:** * Each 3D file type uses its own dedicated JSON file and cannot be used with other types. * e.g., an Export FBX preset cannot be used for Export OBJ * Import and Export used separate dedicated JSON files. * e.g., an Import FBX preset cannot be used for Export FBX

title: Graphic Configuration
content: ### Objective Configure graphics to repeat along the x-axis, y-axis, or all over the pattern. Use this function when graphics are used repeatedly on a Garment. ### Location #### Via the Property Editor Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D Toolbar or 3D Toolbar ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) #### Via the Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Transform Graphic ▶ Right-Click (on 2D Graphic) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Graphic ▶ Right-Click (on 2D Graphic) ### Operation #### Via the Property Editor 1. Follow the path: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D Toolbar or 3D Toolbar ▶ Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) → The properties of the selected graphic will appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the Tile menu in the Property Editor and adjust the settings below as needed: Option | Description ---|--- Revert to Original | Reset the graphic to its original configuration before this function was used. X-Axis | Repeat the graphic along the x-axis of the pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. Y-Axis | Repeat the graphic along the y-axis of the pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. Pattern | Repeat the graphic across the entire pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. → The selected graphic will be tiled according to the menu selection. Via the Right-Click Pop-Up Menu 1. Follow the path: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ Transform Graphic ▶ Right-Click (on 2D Graphic) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Graphic ▶ Right-Click (on 2D Graphic) → Right-click pop-up menu appears. 2. Navigate to Tile and select from the available options (same as Property Editor). → The selected graphic will be tiled according to the menu selection. ※Note: When a graphic is repeated using this function, its Graphic Transformation ▶ Original Width and Original Height values will change.
content_description: This web page provides a guide for configuring the tiling of graphics along the x-axis, y-axis, or across an entire pattern for use on garments, detailing access methods and operational steps through the Property Editor and right-click pop-up menu.
